title: Quotation, paraphrase, summary
must: Quotation = exact words in quotation marks + citation; paraphrase = one idea in own words and structure; summary = main points, much shorter; all need a citation.

title: When to quote, paraphrase or summarise
must: Quote when exact words matter (definition, interview), keep quotes short and few; paraphrase / summarise to show understanding.

title: How to paraphrase correctly
must: Read and understand, close the source, write in own words and sentence structure, compare with the original, add the citation; changing a few words is not a paraphrase.

title: Common knowledge
must: Widely known facts (Astana is the capital) need no citation; statistics, opinions and specific findings do.

title: Referencing systems
must: In-text citation + reference list; Harvard style example (Author, year) and a full reference for a book and a web page (author, title, URL, date accessed).

title: Copyright
must: The exclusive legal right of the author / owner of an original work to copy, distribute, adapt, publish and perform it; arises automatically.

title: Licence and public domain
must: Licence = permission to use under conditions, does not transfer ownership; public domain = copyright expired or given up, free to use.

title: Rules of copyright protection
must: At least three: automatic on creation, lasts the author's life + a set number of years, protects the expression not the idea, © sign not required, owner decides use.

title: Economic and moral rights
must: Economic rights: to earn from the work (copy, sell, license); moral rights: to be named as author and protect the work from distortion — cannot be sold.

title: Free use
must: Allowed without permission: short quotations with source for study / criticism / news, personal use, education within limits.

title: Plagiarism vs copyright infringement
must: Plagiarism = not acknowledging the author (ethical / academic); infringement = using without permission (legal); one can happen without the other.

title: Creative Commons
must: Elements BY, SA, NC, ND with what each means; using CC images in a school project with credit.

title: Software licences
must: EULA, proprietary, open source, freeware, shareware — what each allows.

title: Copyleft vs permissive and software piracy
must: Copyleft (GPL) changes must stay open; permissive (MIT) may be used in closed software; piracy = copying / installing / selling without a licence, e.g. one licence on 30 PCs.
